clause_evidence.reasoning: Samples ask students to provide numerical quantities (how many days or weeks) but do not require descriptive language. The verb describe is minimally employed; students count rather than articulate duration in written or verbal form.
All 22 samples measure duration between two calendar dates as requested. Each sample specifies a start and end date and asks students to determine the span, directly addressing event duration.

While 13 samples ask for day counts, the hints accompanying them contain arithmetic errors. Sample 8b038537589d7d4fee5e hints Subtract: 27 - 24 = 4 days which is mathematically false. This systematic error undermines the validity of day-count instruction.

Nine samples ask for week counts but all contain invalid hint arithmetic. Sample 5dab66adb1f15848ed97 hints Subtract: 10 - 4 = 1 week which is false (10 minus 4 equals 6). This pervasive error makes week-count instruction unreliable.
All 22 samples include a Calendar visual type and require students to read dates from a rendered calendar interface. The visual is present and functional in all samples.
